page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-standard-80 is an x86_64 general-purpose virtual machine designed for high-concurrency workloads requiring balanced CPU and memory resources. Built on dedicated CPU allocation, the instance provides 80 vCPUs paired with 320.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 allocation ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU core.

The hardware configuration does not feature attached local storage or discrete graphics accelerators. Persistent storage must be supplied via network-attached volumes, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default. Compute operations rely entirely on the host x86_64 processors without GPU offloading.

By delivering a dense footprint of 80 vCPUs and 320.0 GB RAM without the financial premium of onboard accelerators or bundled NVMe drives, the n4d-standard-80 offers cost-efficient scaling for compute-and-memory balanced operations. It is well structured for large-scale enterprise microservices, build farms, batch processing systems, container orchestration clusters, and standard database services relying on decoupled persistent disk architecture.

The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions, and does not bundle hardware GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. With its large core count and uniform resource distribution, n4d-standard-80 delivers reliable parallel execution capacity for balanced workloads. By omitting hardware accelerators and bundled physical storage, it maintains resource efficiency for centralized multi-tenant deployments. The server is well suited for running enterprise application servers, large container orchestration nodes, multi-threaded batch jobs, and distributed database services using external block storage.
